verdict.summary: You can create a Dropbox app and connect your own account in minutes, and up to 500 users can link while the app is in development status. Once 50 users have linked, you have two weeks to apply for production status and get approved. If you don't, the app stops accepting new users. The review checks branding, least-privilege scopes and the developer terms, and Dropbox doesn't publish how long it takes.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-3 hours (app setup plus production application, privacy policy and logo)
verdict.approval_wait: none for development use (up to 500 users). Production review time isn't published. You must be approved within 2 weeks of reaching 50 linked users.

gates.name: Development status (your own account)
gates.unlocks: A new app can connect to your own Dropbox account. You can also generate a token in the app's OAuth 2 settings to test the API.
limits: A newly created app can only connect to your own account
A generated token only works for your own account

gates.name: Development status (linked users)
gates.unlocks: Other Dropbox users can link through your OAuth flow without any review.
limits: Up to 500 linked Dropbox users in total
Once 50 users link, you have 2 weeks to apply for and receive production approval. After that, linking new users is frozen, even if some of the 500 slots are unused
Unlinking users does not lift a freeze
Team-linked apps: up to 5 teams in development (community report)
At the cap, users see the error 'This app has reached its user limit.' (community report)

gates.name: Production status
gates.unlocks: Unlimited linked users. Dropbox doesn't document a separate marketplace listing review.
limits: Dropbox may deny the request at its sole discretion
The app name can't be changed after production approval
The app must keep meeting production requirements after approval
Dropbox may set API call limits at its discretion
gates.time_to_reach: Not published. Reviews normally happen around the 50-user mark, or earlier if you use 'Request early review'.

steps.title: Sign in to a Dropbox account
steps.detail: Open the App Console and sign in, or create a Dropbox account. The developer terms require that Dropbox has never terminated an account of yours.

steps.title: Create the app and choose an access type and name
steps.detail: In the App Console, create a new app. Choose 'App folder' access if the app only manages its own content. Choose 'Full Dropbox' if it needs the user's whole Dropbox; apps that use Extensions must choose 'Full Dropbox'. Pick the final name now: it can't include 'Dropbox' or any Dropbox product name, can't start with 'drop' or sound like Dropbox, and can't be changed after production approval.
gotchas: Use one app key per real app. iOS and Android builds of the same app can share a key.
You can't create apps programmatically. Do it by hand in the App Console.

steps.title: Enable only the scopes you need on the Permissions tab
steps.detail: Each endpoint's documentation lists the scope it requires. Use that to work out the smallest set of scopes your agent's tools need, then enable those on the Permissions tab. account_info.read is already on and is required. Composio's default list includes openid, profile and email (OpenID Connect) and the write scopes for files, sharing, file requests and contacts. Remove any you won't use.
gotchas: The scopes enabled here are the most the app can request. Calls to an endpoint without its required scope return an error.
Adding scopes later doesn't update existing grants. Users have to authorize the app again.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI and copy the app key and secret
steps.detail: On the app's Settings tab, add the redirect URI from your Composio auth config under OAuth 2 > Redirect URIs. Then copy the App key (client_id) and App secret (client_secret). If you don't use the implicit grant, turn it off.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URI must exactly match the one registered. Any non-localhost URI must use HTTPS.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config that uses your own app
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom OAuth2 auth config for the dropbox toolkit. Enter your App key and App secret and the same scopes you enabled. Make sure authorization requests include token_access_type=offline. Without it, Dropbox returns only a short-lived access token (the sample shows 14400 seconds) and no refresh token.
gotchas: Refresh tokens don't expire on their own. Refreshing doesn't return a new refresh token, so keep the original one.

steps.title: Connect your own Dropbox account
steps.detail: Run the Composio connect flow with your own account and call a simple endpoint to confirm the token and scopes work. If Dropbox returns unknown_client_id, the app key was entered incorrectly.

steps.title: Let test users link and track the user count
steps.detail: While the app is in development status, up to 500 users can link through OAuth. Check the user count under Analytics in the App Console. Reaching 50 linked users starts a 2-week deadline to get production approval.
gotchas: If you miss the deadline, new links are frozen. Unlinking users doesn't fix this.

steps.title: Prepare the privacy policy, logo and branding review
steps.detail: Write a privacy policy that accurately describes what Dropbox data you collect, how you use it and who you share it with. Prepare an app logo that doesn't include or look like any Dropbox logo. Check that your marketing doesn't suggest a partnership with or endorsement by Dropbox, and uses the Dropbox name only to indicate compatibility.
gotchas: The guide says apps that don't follow the branding guidelines and terms will be rejected.
Publicly searchable file-sharing networks are not allowed.

steps.title: Draft the API-use description and scope justification
steps.detail: Write a detailed description of how the app uses the API, and explain why each enabled scope is needed. If some scopes are for features you haven't built yet, say so. If you need review before reaching 50 users, write the evidence and explanation for the 'Request early review' field.

steps.title: Submit the production status application
steps.detail: In the App Console, fill in the production application form for the app. Upload the app icon and paste in your description, scope justification and, if you want it, the early review request.

steps.title: Wait for Dropbox's decision
steps.detail: Dropbox reviews the request and may deny it at its sole discretion. Review times aren't published. Plan to submit soon after 50 users link so you're approved within the 2-week window.

steps.title: Stay compliant after approval
steps.detail: After approval you can't rename the app, and it must keep meeting production requirements. Report any known or suspected security breach to Dropbox promptly. If you add scopes later, users must authorize the app again.

requirements.item: Signed-in Dropbox account, with no prior account terminated by Dropbox
requirements.detail: You need an account to use the App Console, and the developer terms require this warranty.
The redirect URI must exactly match the one registered in the App Console. Only localhost may use plain HTTP.

requirements.item: App name that follows the branding rules
requirements.detail: No 'Dropbox' or Dropbox product names, can't start with 'drop' or sound like Dropbox, and can't be changed after production approval.
Required in the production application. It must not look like any Dropbox logo.
Must accurately describe what user data you collect and how you use and share it.
The review checks that the app doesn't request broader permissions than it needs.

requirements.item: Users authenticate through Dropbox OAuth, and data is sent over TLS
requirements.detail: Your app must not collect Dropbox login credentials itself, and it must use HTTPS.

scopes.effect: Enabled by default and required for user-linked apps.
Needed to list and read files. Dropbox doesn't classify scopes into tiers, but the review checks that each one is justified.
Write scopes widen what the app can do. Justify each one in the production application or leave it off. Asking for more than you need can hurt the review and lead users to decline.
Used for OpenID Connect sign-in. You must list them explicitly in the scope parameter.
Lets the app act as any team member. Team endpoints must be authorized by a team administrator.

blockers.symptom: New users can't link after the app passes 50 users
blockers.cause: You didn't get production approval within 2 weeks of reaching 50 linked users, so the app is frozen.
blockers.fix: Apply for production status and get approved. Unlinking users won't unfreeze the app.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'This app has reached its user limit.'
blockers.cause: The app has hit its development-status user cap.
The app breaks the branding rules (name or logo) or the developer terms, or requests broader scopes than it needs. Dropbox may also deny requests at its discretion.
blockers.fix: Rename the app and change the logo to meet the branding guide, remove unneeded scopes or justify them, and resubmit with a detailed description.

blockers.symptom: Can't connect more than 5 Dropbox teams
blockers.cause: Team-linked apps in development status are reportedly limited to 5 teams.

blockers.symptom: unknown_client_id error on the authorize page
blockers.cause: The app key in the Composio auth config is wrong.
blockers.fix: Copy the App key from the App Console Settings tab again.

composio.note: Composio's managed Dropbox app is the fastest way to start on prototypes and internal tools. Dropbox's development-status limits (500 users in total, and a freeze 2 weeks after 50 users without approval) apply to whichever app key you use. To distribute to many end users, register your own Dropbox app and get it to production status under your own name and branding. Dropbox's developer guide says tools that wrap its platform for other developers must have those developers use their own app keys. It's unverified whether Composio's shared key has production status.

open_questions: How long does a production review take? Dropbox publishes no timeline or SLA. The only stated timing is the 2-week window after 50 linked users.
Does Composio's managed Dropbox app key have development or production status, and would its approval cover your end users?
Does Composio's custom auth config send token_access_type=offline by default? Without it, there are no refresh tokens.
Are there API rate-limit numbers for development-status apps? None were found beyond the discretionary call cap in the developer terms.
Is there a list of which scopes are sensitive or trigger extra review? None was found.
Does the Dropbox integrations directory have its own listing review? It wasn't checked.
Are security assessments, demo videos or domain verification required? None were found on the pages checked.
The 5-team development cap for team-linked apps comes only from a community answer.
Did the 'Introducing our new Dropbox API documentation' post (Sep 21, 2026) change any of these steps? Its content wasn't read.
